reply:
I reviewed commit f2cdaad, "Retry deliveries until they succeed", and the change is not safe to merge as written. It replaces the three-attempt limit in `deliver` with a loop that never stops and never reports why a send failed.

The change touches one file, `src/queue.js` (3 lines added, 3 removed). The repository has no tests, linter config or `package.json`, so I ran no automated checks; this review comes from reading the code. The commit message only restates the title and there's no linked ticket, so I don't know why the limit was removed.

## Verdict

Verdict: request changes

## Findings

| Severity | Location | Evidence | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocker | `src/queue.js:3` | `while (true) {` | **A message that always fails is retried forever.** Some failures won't go away by retrying: a malformed message, a rejected request, an expired credential. For those, `deliver` never returns or throws, so whatever is waiting on it stalls for good. Before this change the caller got the error after three attempts and could deal with it. Put a limit back (a `maxAttempts` setting, perhaps) and throw the last error once it's reached. |
| blocker | `src/queue.js:3-8` | `return await send(message);` … `// ignore and try again` | **A fast failure can freeze the whole process.** Nothing waits between attempts. If `send` fails immediately (for example, its connection is already closed), the loop keeps itself busy without ever letting timers, network events or other requests run. A single bad message can then lock up the service, and even when `send` fails slowly, the receiving service is retried with no pause. Wait between attempts, increasing the wait each time with some randomness (exponential backoff with jitter). That also gives the rest of the program room to run. |
| major | `src/queue.js:7` | `// ignore and try again` | **Errors are thrown away without being logged.** If deliveries start failing, nobody can tell from logs or metrics, because the queue just looks slow. Log each failed attempt with the attempt number and the error. Ideally, retry only errors that are likely to be temporary (timeouts, overloaded servers) and fail straight away on permanent ones. |
| major | `src/queue.js:2` | `export async function deliver(send, message)` | **The behaviour changed and no tests came with it.** This change makes the old "give up after N tries" behaviour easy to lose without anyone noticing. Add tests for: success on the first try, success after a few temporary failures, and the last error being thrown once the limit is reached. |
| question | `src/queue.js:2` | `deliver` used to throw after the 3rd attempt | Is any code outside this repository relying on `deliver` throwing, for example to move a failed message to a dead-letter queue? Without the throw, that code never runs. |
| minor | commit f2cdaad | `Retry deliveries until they succeed` | The commit message doesn't say why three attempts weren't enough. If messages were being dropped after brief outages, a higher limit with backoff fixes that without the risks above. Saying so in the message would help whoever reads this history later. |

## Strengths

- The header comment was updated to match the new behaviour, so the code and its comment agree.
- The diff contains only this change, which makes it easy to read.

## Deferred

- If losing messages is the real problem, add a dead-letter queue for messages that are still failing at the limit. It belongs in its own ticket, not in this fix.

## Unevaluated

- **Tests:** none exist, so nothing could be run.
- **Linting:** no linter is set up (no ESLint config or `package.json`).
- **Code that calls `deliver`:** none is in this repository, so I couldn't see who depends on the old throw.
- **Report format check:** I couldn't run the skill's script on this report because this session can't save files or run Node.js.
